claims.claim: Aeva's CityOS extends its 4D LiDAR and edge-AI stack into deployable intelligent-transportation infrastructure, broadening the platform beyond vehicle OEM programs into municipal roadway safety and traffic analytics.

Aeva Omni extends the same FMCW platform into compact short-range 360-degree physical-AI sensing; LG Innotek is responsible for hardware integration, manufacturing and quality assurance, creating a distinct manufacturing-partner path from Aeva's long-range automotive programs.

risks: CityOS commercial scale and recurring economics remain undisclosed.
Omni was scheduled for second-half-2026 pilots with production targeted for 2027, so execution remains pre-production.

contradictions.contradiction: Platform breadth is expanding across smart infrastructure and physical AI faster than disclosed scaled economics are becoming visible.

unknowns: CityOS customer count, contract value and recurring revenue contribution.
Omni pilot conversion, committed production volumes and economics.

claims.claim: CityOS was described as available for deployment in March 2026 and was being demonstrated to transportation agencies at ITS America in June, providing an execution checkpoint separate from automotive design wins.

Omni's disclosed roadmap set early customer pilots for the second half of 2026 and production for 2027; these dates are useful forward execution checkpoints rather than evidence of current scaled revenue.

risks: Availability and demonstrations do not establish material bookings or revenue.
Production timing remains forward-looking and subject to qualification/manufacturing risk.

contradictions.contradiction: Broader product availability and demonstrations have not yet resolved the packet's core gap around scaled production economics.

unknowns: Whether second-half-2026 Omni pilots have begun and at what scale.
Whether CityOS deployments have converted into material revenue.
